body: The Airbus A380 remains one of the most recognizable aircraft in commercial aviation, and despite production having ended, the world's largest passenger airliner continues to operate an impressive international network. According to the Simple Flying Flight Tracker, 14,140 A380 movements were recorded between October 5 and November 3, 2026, representing 7,070 individual flights, with each flight counted at both its departure and arrival airports. Dubai International Airport recorded 4,285 flights, substantially more than any other airport, reflecting its role as the primary hub for Emirates; the airline has built much of its international network around the aircraft. Data from ch-aviation shows Emirates is by far the world's largest A380 operator, with 116 aircraft.

London Heathrow saw 1,162 A380 flights, placing it second overall, with six different airlines operating the type: British Airways, Qantas, Emirates, Qatar Airways, Singapore Airlines and Etihad Airways. British Airways, with 12 A380s, is the joint-second largest operator together with Singapore Airlines, and flies the type on selected long-haul services including Miami, San Francisco and Singapore. Singapore Changi followed with 895 flights, served by British Airways, Qantas, Emirates and Singapore Airlines; Singapore Airlines was the launch operator of the A380 in 2007 and still flies it on long-haul operations. Sydney Kingsford Smith recorded 628 flights, operated by Asiana Airlines, Singapore Airlines, Qantas and Emirates.

The remaining airports in the ranking were Bangkok Suvarnabhumi with 356 flights, Los Angeles with 342, Paris Charles de Gaulle with 333, New York John F. Kennedy with 284 and Manchester with 167. Manchester's A380 services are operated solely by Emirates, giving spotters in northern England an alternative to travelling to London. Birmingham, Prague, Denpasar and Christchurch also see daily A380 services from Emirates, while Glasgow receives less frequent visits, showing that the Superjumbo's presence extends well beyond the world's largest connecting hubs.
en.summary: Between October 5 and November 3, 2026, the Airbus A380 flew 7,070 flights worldwide, or 14,140 movements counting each departure and arrival. Dubai International Airport led with 4,285 flights, all operated by Emirates, followed by London Heathrow with 1,162 flights across six airlines, Singapore Changi with 895 and Sydney with 628.
en.title: Where to spot the Airbus A380 in 2026: Dubai leads with 4,285 flights, London Heathrow offers the most airlines

body: 空中巴士A380雖已停產，仍是全球最具代表性的客機之一。根據Simple Flying飛行追蹤器的統計，2026年10月5日至11月3日之間，全球共記錄14,140架次A380起降、相當於7,070個航班；每一個航班在起飛與降落機場各計一次。杜拜國際機場以4,285班遙遙領先，幾乎全數由阿聯酋航空執飛；根據ch-aviation資料，阿聯酋航空擁有116架A380，是全球最大的A380營運商。

倫敦希斯洛以1,162班居次，但航司種類最豐富，共有6家航司執飛，包括英國航空、卡達航空、阿聯酋航空、新加坡航空、澳洲航空與阿提哈德航空；英國航空擁有12架A380，與新加坡航空並列全球第二大營運商，執飛邁阿密、舊金山與新加坡等長程航線。新加坡樟宜以895班居第三，澳洲航空、英國航空、阿聯酋航空與新加坡航空皆有執飛；新加坡航空是2007年A380的首家營運商，至今仍在長程航線使用該機型。雪梨以628班居第四，執飛航司包括韓亞航空、新加坡航空、澳洲航空與阿聯酋航空。
排名其後的機場包括曼谷素萬那普356班、洛杉磯342班、巴黎戴高樂333班、紐約甘迺迪284班與曼徹斯特167班；其中曼徹斯特僅由阿聯酋航空執飛，是英格蘭北部旅客就近欣賞A380的據點。此外，伯明罕、布拉格、丹帕沙與基督城也有阿聯酋航空的每日A380航班，格拉斯哥則班次較少，顯示A380的足跡已超出大型轉運樞紐，延伸至更多中小型機場。
zh.summary: 根據2026年10月5日至11月3日的追蹤統計，全球A380航班共7,070班次、14,140架次起降；杜拜國際機場以4,285班居首且全數為阿聯酋航空執飛，倫敦希斯洛以1,162班居次、共有6家航司執飛，新加坡樟宜與雪梨分居第三、四名。
zh.title: 2026年A380航班最密集的機場：杜拜4,285班居首、倫敦希斯洛航司最多
